exampleAnswers.title: Computing the Derivative of a Product Given the Necessary Data

question.text:
The values of functions $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=-4$ are given in the table below.

$x$ $f(x)$ $g(x)$ $f'(x)$ $g'(x)$
$-4$ $-2$ $-7$ $1$ $10$

Compute $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big(f(x)g(x)\big)$ at $x=-4.$
question.explanation:
Using the product rule, we get

\[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big(f(x)g(x)\big) = f(x)g'(x)+g(x)f'(x). \]

At the point where $x=-4$, this gives

\begin{align} \left.\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big(f(x)g(x)\big)\right|_{x=-4}&=f(-4)g'(-4)+g(-4)f'(-4)\\ &= (-2)\cdot 10 + (-7)\cdot 1 \\[5pt] &= -27. \end{align}

example.title: Computing the Derivative of a Product Given the Necessary Data

question.text:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you're given the following data:

\[ f(0)= 5, \quad f'(0)=-2, \quad g(0)=10, \quad g'(0)=4 \]

Compute $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big(f(x)g(x)\big)$ at $x=0.$
question.explanation:
Using the product rule, we get

\[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big(f(x)g(x)\big) = f(x)g'(x)+g(x)f'(x). \]

At the point where $x=0,$ this gives

\begin{align*} \left.\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big(f(x)g(x)\big)\right|_{x=0} &= f(0)g'(0)+g(0)f'(0)\\ &= 5 \cdot 4+10 \cdot (-2) \\[5pt] &= 0. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Computing the Derivative of a Quotient Given the Necessary Data

question.text:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you are given the following data:

\[ f(-4)= 2e, \quad f'(-4)=-e, \quad g(-4)=-3e, \quad g'(-4)=e \]

Compute $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}\right)$ at $x=-4.$
question.explanation:
Using the quotient rule, we get \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}\right) = \dfrac{f'(x)g(x)-f(x)g'(x)}{(g(x))^2}. \]

At the point where $x=-4,$ this gives

\begin{align*} \left.\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}\right)\right|_{x=-4} &= \dfrac{f'(-4)g(-4)-f(-4)g'(-4)}{g^2(-4)}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{ -e \cdot (-3e) - 2e \cdot e}{ 9e^2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac 19. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing the Derivative of a Quotient Given the Necessary Data

question.text:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you are given the following data:

\[ f(-2)=1, \quad f'(-2)=-3, \quad g(-2)=2, \quad g'(-2)=6 \]

Compute $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}\right)$ at $x=-2.$
question.explanation:
Using the quotient rule, we get \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}\right) = \dfrac{f'(x)g(x)-f(x)g'(x)}{(g(x))^2}. \]

At the point where $x=-2$, this gives

\begin{align*} \left.\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\left(\dfrac{f(x)}{g(x)}\right)\right|_{x=-2}&=\dfrac{f'(-2)g(-2)-f(-2)g'(-2)}{g^2(-2)}\\[5pt] &=\dfrac{(-3) \cdot 2 - 1 \cdot 6}{2^2}\\[5pt] &=-3. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Computing the Derivative of a Linear Combination of Functions Given the Necessary Data

question.text:
For the functions $g(x)$ and $u(x),$ you're given the following data:

\[ g(-2)=-6, \quad g'(-2)=3, \quad u(-2)=4, \quad u'(-2)=-8 \]

Compute $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big( 2g(x) + u(x) \big)$ at $x=-2.$
question.explanation:
Using the sum and constant multiple rules, we get \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big( 2g(x) + u(x) \big) = 2g'(x) + u'(x). \]

At the point where $x=-2$, this gives

\begin{align*} \left.\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big( 2g(x) + u(x) \big)\right|_{x=-2} &= 2g'(-2) + u'(-2) \\[5pt] &= 2\cdot 3 + (-8) \\[5pt] &= 6 - 8 \\[5pt] &= -2. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing the Derivative of a Linear Combination of Functions Given the Necessary Data

question.text:
The values of functions $q(x)$ and $r(x)$ and their derivatives at $x=2$ are given in the table below.

$x$ $q(x)$ $r(x)$ $q'(x)$ $r'(x)$
$2$ $4$ $-1$ $-3$ $2$

Compute $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big(3q(x)+4r(x)\big)$ at $x=2.$
question.explanation:
Using the sum and constant multiple rules, we get \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big(3q(x)+4r(x)\big) = 3q'(x)+4r'(x). \]

At the point where $x=2$, this gives \[ \begin{align*} \left.\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big(3q(x)+4r(x)\big)\right|_{x=2} &= 3q'(2)+4r'(2) \\[5pt] &= 3(-3)+4(2) \\[5pt] &= -9+8 \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{-1}. \end{align*} \]

example.title: Computing the Derivative of a Linear Combination of Functions Given the Necessary Data

question.text:
For the functions $e(x)$ and $n(x),$ you're given the following data:

\[ e(-5)=5, \quad e'(-5)=-6, \quad n(-5)=-7, \quad n'(-5)=9 \]

Compute $\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big( 3e(x) + n(x) \big)$ at $x=-5.$
question.explanation:
Using the sum and constant multiple rules, we get \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big( 3e(x) + n(x) \big) = 3e'(x) + n'(x). \]

At the point where $x=-5$, this gives

\begin{align*} \left.\dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x}\big( 3e(x) + n(x) \big)\right|_{x=-5} &= 3e'(-5) + n'(-5) \\[5pt] &= 3\cdot (-6) + 9 \\[5pt] &= -18 + 9 \\[5pt] &= -9. \end{align*}

exampleAnswers.title: Computing the Derivative of the Product or Quotient of a Composition of Functions Given the Necessary Data

question.text:
The values of functions $h(t)$ and $z(t)$ and their derivatives at $t=4$ are given in the table below.

$t$ $h(t)$ $z(t)$ $h'(t)$ $z'(t)$
$4$ $1$ $-2$ $3$ $1$

If $f(t) = \dfrac{2h(t)-5}{1-z(t)},$ compute $f'(4).$ Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
The quotient rule states that \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\Big( \dfrac{u}{v} \Big) = \dfrac{u'v - uv'}{v^2}. \]

Let $u = 2h(t) - 5$ and $v = 1 - z(t).$ Differentiating each, we get \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}u}{\textrm{d}t} = 2h'(t) \qquad \text{and} \qquad \dfrac{\textrm{d}v}{\textrm{d}t} = -z'(t). \]

Substituting into the quotient rule gives

\[ f'(t) = \dfrac{2h'(t)(1 - z(t)) - (2h(t) - 5)(-z'(t))}{(1 - z(t))^2}. \]

At $t=4,$ this gives

\[ \begin{align*} f'(4) & = \dfrac{2h'(4)(1 - z(4)) - (2h(4) - 5)(-z'(4))}{(1 - z(4))^2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2(3)(1 - (-2)) - (2(1) - 5)(-1)}{(1 - (-2))^2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{2(3)(3) - (-3)(-1)}{(3)^2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{18 - 3}{9} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{15}{9} \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{5}{3}}. \end{align*} \]

example.title: Computing the Derivative of the Product or Quotient of a Composition of Functions Given the Necessary Data

question.text:
The values of functions $h(x)$ and $z(x)$ and their derivatives at $t=3$ are given in the table below.

$t$ $h(t)$ $z(t)$ $h'(t)$ $z'(t)$
$3$ $-2$ $6$ $5$ $-1$

If $f(t) = \dfrac{2+h(t)}{z(t)},$ compute $f'(3).$ Do not round the answer.
question.explanation:
The quotient rule states that \[ \dfrac{\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}t}\left(\dfrac uv\right) = \dfrac{u'v-uv'}{v^2}. \]

Let $u=2+h(t)$ and $v=z(t).$ Differentiating each, we get \[ \dfrac{\textrm d u}{\textrm d t} = h'(t) \qquad \text{and} \qquad \dfrac{\textrm d v}{\textrm d t} = z'(t). \]

Substituting into the quotient rule gives \[ f'(t) = \dfrac{h'(t)z(t) - (2+h(t))z'(t)}{z^2(t)}. \]

At $t=3,$ this gives \[ \begin{align*} f'(3) &= \dfrac{h'(3)z(3) - (2+h(3))z'(3)}{z^2(3)} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{5\cdot 6 - (2+(-2))(-1)}{6^2} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{30-(0)(-1)}{36} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{30}{36} \\[5pt] &= \bbox[4pt,border: 1px solid lightgray]{\dfrac{5}{6}}. \end{align*} \]
